source.title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let k be a fixed positive integer and let F_d^k(D_d) be the class of functions f:D_d -> R on a domain D_d subset R^d of volume 1 such that every mixed partial derivative D^alpha f of order |alpha| <= k satisfies ||D^alpha f||_infty <= 1. For which domains D_d does the worst-case integration error admit an upper bound of the form e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) <= c_k d n^(-k/d), and how can one explicitly construct algorithms that achieve this rate on those domains?
accepted.context_brief: Domain-dependent upper bounds for classical smoothness classes

evidence.quote: Open Problem: For which Dd do we have upper bounds of the form e(n,Fkd (Dd)) <= ckdn-k/d ? Construct algorithms that achieve this bound for such domains.

accepted.question_text: For randomized numerical integration on the classical smoothness classes F_d^k = {f:[0,1]^d -> R : ||D^alpha f||_infty <= 1 for every multi-index alpha with |alpha| <= k}, upper bounds of the form d^t n^(-k/d-1/2) are known. What is the smallest possible exponent t in the dimension factor d^t for such randomized upper bounds?

evidence.quote: Open Problem: Study, similarly as in Theorem 1, the dependence on the dimension for randomized algorithms. Using results of Krieg [53] one can prove upper bounds of the form dt n-k/d-1/2. One may take t = (k+1)/2, but the optimal (smallest) t is not known.

accepted.question_text: In tensor-product numerical integration problems on reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, assume for each coordinate space H_i there is a unit-norm bounded linear functional with nonnegative representer h_i, functions f_i and g_i such that (h_i,f_i,g_i) is orthonormal, and a parameter alpha_i in (0,1] such that alpha_i h_i = sqrt(f_i^2+g_i^2). Under these assumptions the worst-case error satisfies lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_{i=1}^d (1+alpha_i^2)^(-1). Do analogous lower bounds hold for comparable integration problems on Banach spaces rather than Hilbert spaces?
accepted.context_brief: Banach-space analogues of Hilbert-space lower bounds

evidence.quote: Theorem 2. [42]. For all i <= d, let Hi be a RKHS and let S~i be a bounded linear functional on Hi with unit norm and nonnegative representer hi. ... Then the tensor product problem Sd = S~1 \u2297...\u2297S~d satisfies for all n \u2208 N that e(n,Fd)2 >= 1-n prod_{i=1}^d (1+alpha_i^2)^-1.
Open Problem: The lower bounds of [42] are for Hilbert spaces. Do similar lower bounds exist for Banach spaces?

accepted.question_text: For one-dimensional numerical integration, two universal randomized strategies are highlighted: a randomly shifted midpoint rule with a random number n in {m,m+1,...,2m} for periodic functions, and, for non-periodic functions, a method that first interpolates f at Chebyshev points by a polynomial f_m and then applies separation of the main part together with Monte Carlo to f-f_m. How do these two approaches compare in detail, both theoretically and practically, in dimension d=1?

evidence.quote: We start with the simplest case: Periodic functions on [0,1], hence d = 1. Then a very simple algorithm has many optimality properties: Pick n \u2208 {m,m + 1,m + 2,...,2m} randomly and then take a randomly shifted midpoint rule with n function values and equal weights.

As an alternative, one can take n = 2m and first define, via interpolation at the Chebyshev points, a polynomial fm of degree smaller than m. Then we use separation of the main part together with the simplest Monte Carlo method for (f - fm) to obtain an almost optimal algorithm for each class Fk1.
Open Problem: Study and compare these algorithms (for d = 1) in more detail.

accepted.question_text: A universal integration algorithm is meant to perform optimally across multiple smoothness classes rather than being tuned to one specific class. Here tractability concerns how the information complexity n(epsilon,F_d) depends on dimension d and error tolerance epsilon, for example polynomial dependence on d and epsilon^(-1), or strong polynomial dependence on epsilon^(-1) alone. Can universality be developed at the level of tractability as well, so that one studies and characterizes universal algorithms with optimal tractability properties, not only optimal convergence rates?

evidence.quote: If n(epsilon,F_d) is bounded by a polynomial in d and epsilon^{-1} then we say that the problem is polynomially tractable. If n(epsilon,F_d) is bounded by a polynomial in epsilon^{-1} alone ... then we say that the problem is strongly polynomially tractable.

For classical smoothness k > d/2 eran(An,Hkd) \u224d n-k/d-1/2 and e(An,Hkd) \u224d n-k/d. For mixed smoothness k \u2208 N eran(An,Hk,mixd) \u224d n-k-1/2 and e(An,Hk,mixd) \u224d n-k (log n)(d-1)/2. All these orders of convergence are optimal.
Open Problem: Of course one should study universality for tractability questions, not only for the rate of convergence.

accepted.question_text: Universal algorithms for multivariate integration have been constructed for the cube [0,1]^d. Do there exist universal algorithms of the same kind for integration over domains other than [0,1]^d?

evidence.quote: Open Problem: So far only the domain [0,1]d was studied for the construction of universal algorithms. One might speculate that universal algorithms also exist for other domains.

accepted.question_text: For the classical smoothness classes F_d^k(D_d) on volume-1 domains, explicit lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) >= min{1/2, c_k d n^(-k/d)} are known. What are the sharp values or sharper estimates of the constants c_k, and which domains D_d are extremal in the sense that, for given k, d, and n, the integration error e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) is especially small?

evidence.quote: We know from [47] the following statement for the classes Fkd (Dd) = { f : Dd -> R | ||Dalpha f||infty <= 1, |alpha| <= k} for all domains Dd with volume 1: For all k \u2208 N there exists a constant ck > 0 such that for all d,n \u2208 N e(n,Fkd (Dd)) >= min{1/2, ck d n-k/d}.

Remark 7. 1) The lower bound cannot be improved since for cubes we have a similar upper bound. It would be good to know more on the constants ck and on extremal sets Dd, where e(n,Fkd (Dd )) is small for given k, d and n.

accepted.question_text: Fix d and let D_d be a Jordan measurable domain of volume 1. For the classical smoothness classes F_d^k(D_d), does the asymptotic constant C_{D_d} = lim_{n->infinity} e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) n^(k/d) exist, and if it exists, is it independent of the particular shape of D_d, perhaps under suitable assumptions on the boundary?

evidence.quote: It is known that the weak order e(n,Fkd (Dd)) \u224d n-k/d holds at least for every bounded Lipschitz domain.

We guess that more is true and the asymptotic constant lim n->infty e(n,Fkd (Dd)) \u00b7 nk/d = CDd does not depend on Dd (for fixed d) if Dd is Jordan measurable with \u03bbd(Dd) = 1; possibly under some assumptions on the boundary of Dd.

accepted.question_text: Let C_tilde^2(D_d) be the class of twice continuously differentiable functions f on an open set D_d subset R^d with volume 1 such that ||f||_infty <= 1, Lip(f) <= d^(-1/2), and every directional derivative D^Theta f satisfies Lip(D^Theta f) <= d^(-1) for all directions Theta on the unit sphere. Does there exist a constant C>0, independent of d and of the domain D_d, such that the worst-case integration error always satisfies e(n,C_tilde^2(D_d)) >= C n^(-2/d)?
accepted.context_brief: Conjectured lower bound for an orthogonally invariant C2 class

evidence.quote: Example 1. Let us discuss the integration problem for the class C~2(Dd) = { f \u2208 C2(Dd) | ||f||infty <= 1, Lip(f) <= d-1/2, Lip(DTheta f) <= d-1 }, as in [45, 46, 48].
We conjecture that there exists a constant C > 0 (independent on d and Dd) such that e(n,C~2(Dd)) >= C \u00b7 n-2/d.

accepted.question_text: For the same orthogonally invariant class C_tilde^2(D_d), it is known that the integration problem suffers from the curse of dimensionality for certain domains D_d having small radius, including l_p^d balls with p>=2. Does the curse of dimensionality also hold when D_d is an l_p^d ball with p<2?
accepted.context_brief: Curse of dimensionality on lp balls

evidence.quote: It is known that the integration problem for C~2(Dd) and certain Dd suffers from the curse of dimensionality. This is true if Dd has a small radius, see [48] for the best known results. For example, the curse is known if Dd is a lpd ball and p >= 2. It is not known for p balls and p < 2.

accepted.question_text: For functions with mixed smoothness on the d-torus, specifically the space H_d^{k,mix}(T^d), independent uniformly distributed sample points are known to be optimal for the Monte Carlo error and optimal up to a logarithmic factor for the uniform error, which also yields logarithmic-factor optimality for integration. Can that logarithmic loss be removed for uniformly distributed samples, as happens in the isotropic-smoothness setting?
accepted.context_brief: Mixed-smoothness logarithmic loss under iid sampling

evidence.quote: There are recent results in this direction for the special case of L2-approximation on the Hilbert space Hk,mix(Td) of functions with mixed smoothness k on the d-torus. Namely, it is known that independent and uniformly distributed sampling points are optimal with respect to the Monte Carlo error [54] and optimal up to a logarithmic factor with respect to the uniform error [20, 61, 113].

This also implies that they are optimal up to logarithmic factors for the problem of integration on Hk,mix(Td) with respect to both error criteria. We do not know whether the logarithmic loss can be avoided with uniformly distributed samples, as it is the case with isotropic smoothness. This is another Open Problem.

accepted.question_text: If one restricts numerical integration or approximation algorithms to use iid sample points, what tractability properties can still be achieved? More precisely, how should one characterize and prove tractability results for algorithms based on iid samples, and how do these iid tractability properties differ from the tractability of algorithms using optimally chosen information?

evidence.quote: Open Problem: In this section we presented results on the optimal order of convergence if we may only use iid sample points. There are other ways to compare the power of different algorithms. In particular, one should study "iid tractability", i.e., tractability properties of algorithms that are based on iid sample points, see also [72, 97].
We already know that tractability properties are not related to optimal order of convergence, so there is much room for new research.

accepted.question_text: For Sobolev approximation based on iid uniformly distributed sample points on a domain D_d subset R^d, do the asymptotic constants in expressions such as lim_{n->infinity} e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d)) n^{s/d-(1/p-1/q)+} always exist, and if they exist, do they depend only on the volume of D_d rather than on its shape?

evidence.quote: One possibility is to study the asymptotic constants, such as lim n->infty e(Pn,Wsp(Dd),Lq(Dd )) \u00b7 ns/d-(1/p-1/q)+.
We conjecture that all these asymptotic constants exist and possibly they do not depend on the shape of Dd, only on its volume.

accepted.question_text: Let S_d(f)=integral_{D_d} f(x) rho(x) dx be a weighted multivariate integral over an open set D_d subset R^d, and consider randomized cubature rules of the form A_n^omega(f)=sum_{j=1}^n a_j(omega) f(x_j(omega)), possibly with the sample points x_j chosen as iid uniform points in D_d. Does there exist a universal randomized algorithm for this weighted integration problem, meaning a single algorithm family that works across multiple smoothness classes, with error bounds comparable to those known in the unweighted cube case, perhaps allowing additional logarithmic factors if exact optimal rates are too expensive in practice?

evidence.quote: Study the approximation of the integral Sd(f) = \u222b_Dd f(x)\u03c1(x) dx over an open subset Dd \u2282 Rd for integrable functions f : Dd -> R. We are interested in universal randomized algorithms (A\u03c9n) of the form A\u03c9n(f) = \u2211_{j=1}^n aj(\u03c9)f(xj(\u03c9)), possibly based on iid uniformly distributed xj.

Ideally, we would like to have the same optimal error bounds as in Theorem 3. It is not clear whether such algorithms exist, we know it only for \u03c1 = 1 on Dd = [0,1]d. In addition, the optimal order of convergence may be useless if the involved constants are huge. It might be more practical to relax the order of the error bounds and to allow additional log factors.

needs_review.question_text_raw: For spaces of functions with dominating mixed smoothness many problems are still open.

evidence.quote: For spaces of functions with dominating mixed smoothness many problems are still open, see Triebel [111].

needs_review.question_text_raw: Oscillatory integrals are important for applications and are well studied in numerical analysis. There exist error bounds but only few complexity results (lower bounds and fitting upper bounds).

evidence.quote: Oscillatory integrals are important for applications and are well studied in numerical analysis. There exist error bounds but only few complexity results (lower bounds and fitting upper bounds).

trace.notes: Normalized the original zbMATH URL https://zbmath.org/8011714. zbMATH API metadata identified the exact work as title Optimal algorithms for numerical integration: recent results and open problems, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-59762-6_5, with arXiv full-text link 2307.06787.

Direct local curl attempts to arXiv PDF and the author-uploaded PDF failed with DNS resolution errors, so the exact-title author-uploaded ResearchGate full-text HTML was used as the readable source. Mapped sections 1 Introduction, 2 Lower Bounds, 3 Universality, 4 General Domains, 5 iid Information, and 6 Concluding Remarks; open-problem regions occur primarily in lines 659-664, 918-939, 1313-1319, 1483, 1711-1726, 2061-2150, 2227-2285, 3490-3565, and 3884-3937.
Extracted explicit lower-bound and randomized-dimension open problems from Lower Bounds, including the Banach-space analogue question.
Extracted open problems on comparing one-dimensional universal algorithms, universality for tractability, and universality on domains beyond the cube.
Extracted conjectures and implicit questions on constants, extremal domains, asymptotic constants, and orthogonally invariant C^2 classes on general domains.
Extracted mixed-smoothness, iid tractability, and iid asymptotic-constant questions from the iid Information section.
Extracted the final explicit open problem on weighted integrals and flagged the oscillatory-integral discussion as too broad for acceptance without a narrower statement.

Rewrote 14 accepted items into standalone questions, inlining definitions of function classes, domains, error criteria, iid sampling, tractability, and weighted randomized cubature where supported by source evidence.

No near-duplicate clusters were merged; domain upper bounds, randomized dimension dependence, Banach-space lower bounds, universality, general-domain constants, iid sampling, and weighted-integral questions are distinct.

Accepted items passed self-containedness, evidence coverage, evidence completeness, no-new-facts, source adequacy, solved-status, and schema gates. Two broad statements were moved to needs_review for insufficiently precise question statements.
